conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Report counters
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.15.4 "are not affected by the processing of a dummy report group" -> OK 5); --check 14.9.45.4 "Any changes to LINE-COUNTER associated with the report group" -> OK 3) d). PresentBody returns before any fit test / line / NEXT GROUP for lines.Length==0 and for all-absent PRESENT WHEN, and for a SUPPRESSed instance runs only the sum reset; PH/PF/RH/RF return on SUPPRESS before placement/ApplyNextGroup. Probe a2.cob: GENERATE DS (LINE PLUS 5, NEXT GROUP PLUS 3, suppressed via USE BEFORE REPORTING) leaves LC=3 PC=1 (B) - no page-fit advance although 3+5 > LAST DETAIL 8, no NEXT GROUP; GENERATE DUM (TYPE DE, no LINE) leaves LC=3 PC=1 (C). No existing test observes the counters across a suppressed or dummy group (rw_suppress pins the sum behaviour only) - test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 1985 (Report Writer optional module), 2002, 2014, 2023 - clause 8.4.3.15 text; the SUPPRESS half requires the §14.9.45 SUPPRESS statement]
rows.rule-text: The values of PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER are not affected by the processing of a dummy report group, nor by the processing of a report group whose printing is suppressed by means of the SUPPRESS statement.

rows.subject: Report description entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 13.14.4 OK): 'If GLOBAL is specified, report-name-1 and all its constituent report groups, its PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER, and any sum counters defined in report-name-1 are global.' Code: reportGlobalClause sets ReportModel.IsGlobal; InheritGlobalReport adds the report (and through it its groups and counters) to a contained program's VisibleReports and registers its sum counters, hideable by a local declaration (§8.4.6). Probe g1.cob (2023 and --std 85): contained program reads unqualified PAGE-COUNTER (=01), LINE-COUNTER OF R-1 (=02) and GENERATEs DET-1 IN R-1 of the container's GLOBAL report; output correct. Sum-counter half read in InheritGlobalReport and covered by unit GlobalReportScopeTests.AGlobalReportsSumCounter_IsVisibleInAContainedProgram_UnlessHidden (emit-shape only). conformance:85/pb369_global_report_use_selection covers report-name, groups and PAGE-COUNTER OF R-1 but not LINE-COUNTER or a sum-counter value, so no single spec-derived test covers the whole rule -> test-ref left empty (test-needed).
rows.rule-text: If GLOBAL is specified, report-name-1 and all its constituent report groups, its PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER, and any sum counters defined in report-name-1 are global.

rows.subject: Report group description entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: 'Report group description entries may appear only in the report section.' Structural: `reportGroupEntry` is referenced only from `reportDescriptionEntry : RD reportName reportDescriptionClause* DOT reportGroupEntry*`, and that is referenced only from `reportSection`. Report-group clauses written in WORKING-STORAGE (probe sr1ws: `01 WX TYPE DE. 03 LINE 1. 05 COLUMN 1 PIC X SOURCE WA.`) are refused at parse (COBOL0001 unexpected 'DE', COBOL0307 at LINE/SOURCE). cite.py --check 13.15.3 'Report group description entries may appear only in the report section' -> OK. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the report group description entry is Report Writer nucleus syntax at every edition; no Annex E item changes §13.15 between 2014 and 2023)
rows.rule-text: Report group description entries may appear only in the report section.

rows.subject: Report group description entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: 'The first entry that follows a report description entry shall be a level 1 entry.' BindReportEntry refuses any entry reached while `st.Group` is null, i.e. before the RD's first level-1 entry. Probe sr4 (`03 LINE 1. 05 COLUMN 1 ...` right after the RD) is refused. Two quality notes that do not change the verdict. (1) The error is reported once per leading entry (two errors for two entries). (2) The descriptor sits on the shared COBOLNET0899 'recognized but not implemented' code (DiagnosticCatalog `ReportGroupBefore01 = new(NotImplemented, ...)`, iso 'ISO §13.15') and not on a syntax-rule code, so an illegal-source refusal reads as a staged feature. ReportColumnWithoutLine (SR9) and ReportItemMissingPicture (SR12) have the same misfiling. cite.py --check 13.15.3 'The first entry that follows a report description entry shall be a level 1 entry' -> OK. No spec-derived negative golden pins it, so test-ref is empty. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the report group description entry is Report Writer nucleus syntax at every edition; no Annex E item changes §13.15 between 2014 and 2023) || Code-location detail (moved from the field by registrar 14e): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs#BindReportEntry (DiagnosticCatalog.ReportGroupBefore01)
rows.rule-text: The first entry that follows a report description entry shall be a level 1 entry.

rows.subject: Report group description entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: 'Each level 1 entry identifies a report group. The report group is defined by this entry and all its subordinate entries.' BindReportEntry opens a new ReportGroupModel on `level == 1` (int.TryParse, so `1` and `01` are the same). BindReportEntries computes each entry's subtree as the following entries of a higher level-number. ScreenReportEntryClausePresence derives elementary-ness from that same hierarchy. Probe gr1lvl (`1 D1 TYPE DE. 3 LINE 1. 5 COLUMN 1 ... 1 D2 TYPE DE. 3 LINE PLUS 1. 5 COLUMN 3 ...`, GENERATE D1 then D2) printed `A` on line 1 and `  B` on line 2: two groups, each built from its own subordinates. cite.py --check 13.15.4 'Each level 1 entry identifies a report group' -> OK. No existing spec-derived test is aimed at GR1 alone, so test-ref is empty. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the report group description entry is Report Writer nucleus syntax at every edition; no Annex E item changes §13.15 between 2014 and 2023)
rows.rule-text: Each level 1 entry identifies a report group. The report group is defined by this entry and all its subordinate entries.

rows.subject: Report section
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 13.8.3 OK): the report section may be in a function or program definition; in a class only in a factory or instance definition, never in a method; never in an interface. Every half checked: program — many goldens; function definition — probe c2.cob (FUNCTION-ID with FD/RD/GENERATE) runs, R=1, report file holds FN; factory — probe c4.cob runs, F-DONE, file holds FAC; instance — conformance:2023/oo_object_report; method — DataBinder.Oo.cs emits COBOLNET1519 "a method definition shall not contain a REPORT SECTION" (conformance-test:OoSpineTests.MethodMayNotOwnEnvOrFileSection_1519 covers this half only); interface — interfaceDefinition has no dataDivision, so c5.cob (INTERFACE-ID with DATA DIVISION. REPORT SECTION.) is rejected (generic COBOL0001 parse error, not a targeted diagnostic), and an interface's method prototype's REPORT SECTION is refused by PrototypeUnitRules rule e). Test-ref empty: no single spec-derived test covers the function/factory/interface halves. Open PB1044 (a method's USE BEFORE REPORTING never runs in an instance definition with an RD) cites 13.8.3 but is a runtime/emit defect, not this syntax rule. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO/function-definition clauses of the rule; a program-definition report section is 1985 too) || Code-location detail (moved from the field by registrar 14e): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Oo.cs#BindMethod (COBOLNET1519 REPORT SECTION arm, line ~289) | src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/PrototypeUnitRules.cs (rule e) || Code-location witnesses adjusted by registrar 14e: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Oo.cs#BindMethod (symbol not in the file at 071ff04ea; path kept)
rows.rule-text: The report section may be specified in a function definition or a program definition. Within a class definition, the report section may be specified only in a factory definition or an instance definition, but not in a method definition. The report section shall not be specified within an interface definition.

rows.subject: SAME AS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR2 "A data description entry that specifies the SAME AS clause shall not be immediately followed by a subordinate data description entry or level 88 entry." (--check 13.18.49.3 -> OK 2)). ExpandSameAs: `item.Children.Count > 0 || item.Own88s.Count > 0` -> COBOLNET1555 before the copy. Both halves verified: subordinate half by SameAsTests.SameAsWithSubordinate_Rejected1555; level-88 half by probe p11_sr2_88 (`01 W SAME AS E. 88 W-ON VALUE 1.` -> COBOLNET1555 citing SR2). test-ref left empty: the existing test covers only the subordinate half, the 88 half has no test. Cosmetic: every SAME AS rejection that returns before the copy also emits a cascade COBOLNET0881 (PICTURE required) on the uncopied subject. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME AS clause is absent from COBOL-85 and is not in Annex E's 2014->2023 substantive-changes list, so the rule stands unchanged in 2014 and 2023)
rows.rule-text: A data description entry that specifies the SAME AS clause shall not be immediately followed by a subordinate data description entry or level 88 entry.

rows.subject: SAME AS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR4 "The description of data-name-1, including its subordinate data items, shall not contain a TYPE clause that references the record to which this entry is subordinate." (--check 13.18.49.3 -> OK 4)). The only record a TYPE clause can reference is a TYPEDEF record, so SR4's shape is a SAME AS inside a type declaration whose data-name-1 is (or contains) TYPE of that declaration. No dedicated check exists: the rejection falls out of ExpandType cloning the template's SAME AS subordinate under data-name-1, where the SR3 ancestor walk fires. Probe p05_sr4 (`01 T TYPEDEF. 05 A PIC X. 05 B SAME AS X.` / `01 X TYPE T.`) -> COBOLNET1557 (whose catalog entry names SR3/SR4), but the message text cites SR3 rather than SR4. Since data-name-1 containing TYPE T always reproduces the SAME AS under data-name-1, every SR4 violation is caught by this route; the SR3 wording is cosmetic. No test. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME AS clause is absent from COBOL-85 and is not in Annex E's 2014->2023 substantive-changes list, so the rule stands unchanged in 2014 and 2023)
rows.rule-text: The description of data-name-1, including its subordinate data items, shall not contain a TYPE clause that references the record to which this entry is subordinate.

rows.subject: SAME AS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR6 (--check 13.18.49.3 -> OK 6)). `IsFileSectionItem(item) && HasObjectReferenceLeaf(target)` -> COBOLNET1556; HasObjectReferenceLeaf recurses the subordinates ('including its subordinate data items'). Probes: p13_sr6 (FD record `01 FR SAME AS OREF`, OREF USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE) -> 1556 SR6; p14_sr6grp (object reference inside the group target) -> 1556 SR6; p15_sr6ws (same copy in WORKING-STORAGE) compiles and runs - the file-section condition is honoured. A pending nested SAME AS inside the target is re-screened when CloneItem expands it at the file-section position. No SR6-specific test (negative/pb183-usage-pointer-same-as is §13.18.60.3 SR14, a different rule). || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME AS clause is absent from COBOL-85 and is not in Annex E's 2014->2023 substantive-changes list, so the rule stands unchanged in 2014 and 2023)
rows.rule-text: When the SAME AS clause is specified in the file section, the description of data-name-1, including its subordinate data items, shall not contain a data item described with a USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE clause.

rows.subject: SAME AS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR2 a/b/c (--check 13.18.49.4 -> OK 2) a) and 2) c)). a) CloneItem reproduces names, descriptions (CopyEntryDescription scope Entry), OCCURS, REDEFINES, INDEXED BY, 88s and hierarchy; b) levelDelta = item.Level - target.Level renumbers; c) no 49 cap - probe p10 (`01 T. 49 L PIC 9. 88 L-ON`; `01 O. 10 S SAME AS T.` -> L at level 58; SET L-ON OF S TO TRUE -> [1], FUNCTION LENGTH(O)=1). The NOTE on 8.5.1.6.4 alignment is informative. typedef_same_as covers a) and b) (INNER-REC at 05 copying a level-1 group; CUST-ID OF INNER-REC etc.) but not c) or the copied 88s, so test-ref is left empty (test-needed for the >49 arm). || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME AS clause is absent from COBOL-85 and is not in Annex E's 2014->2023 substantive-changes list, so the rule stands unchanged in 2014 and 2023)
rows.rule-text: If data-name-1 describes a group item: a) the subject of the entry is a group whose subordinate elements have the same names, descriptions, and hierarchy as the subordinate elements of data-name-1, b) the level-numbers of items subordinate to that group are adjusted, if necessary, to preserve the hierarchy of data-name-1, c) level-numbers in the resulting hierarchy may exceed 49. NOTE If alignment according to 8.5.1.6.4, Item alignment for increased object-code efficiency, inserts implicit fillers in either data-name-1 or the subject of the entry, the alignment of the corresponding data items may differ.

rows.subject: SAME AS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR4 "If a group item to which data-name-1 is subordinate contains a GROUP-USAGE clause and the subject of the entry is a group item, the effect is as if that GROUP-USAGE clause had been specified for the subject of the entry." (--check 13.18.49.4 -> OK 4)). PREMISE CHECK: the antecedent cannot be satisfied. SR7 limits data-name-1 to an elementary item or a LEVEL-1 group; a level-1 group has no superordinate group, and an elementary data-name-1 gives an elementary subject (GR1/GR2 - the subject is a group only when data-name-1 is), so 'data-name-1 subordinate to a group' and 'subject is a group' never hold together. Probe r02_gr4 (the only shape that could satisfy it - a level-05 group inside a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL record) is refused by the SR7 guard (COBOLNET1556). The compiler has no GR4 transfer code and needs none; data-name-1's OWN GROUP-USAGE travels via CopyEntryDescription (pb522 golden). Vacuous-conforming; nothing to test. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME AS clause is absent from COBOL-85 and is not in Annex E's 2014->2023 substantive-changes list, so the rule stands unchanged in 2014 and 2023)
rows.rule-text: If a group item to which data-name-1 is subordinate contains a GROUP-USAGE clause and the subject of the entry is a group item, the effect is as if that GROUP-USAGE clause had been specified for the subject of the entry.

rows.subject: SAME SORT/SORT-MERGE AREA clause (extent of allocation)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Voluntary row (A.1 169: internal procedure need not be documented). cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 'The extent of such allocation shall be specified by the implementor' -> OK §12.4.6.4.4 4) b). Code: DataBinder.BindIoControl line ~1801 'if (clause.sameClause() is not { } same || same.RECORD() is null) continue;' — only SAME RECORD AREA binds; sort-merge-area format has no storage effect. Probe probe/p169/s2.cob (SAME SORT AREA FOR SF1 SF2 PLF, two SORTs USING/GIVING PLF) -> CCC BBB AAA at --std 85 and 2023. No spec-derived test pins it (NIST ST13x corroborate only). Adjacent open SR under-rejection kb/Work/PB1087 is a different rule set. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535.
rows.rule-text: SAME SORT/SORT-MERGE AREA clause (extent of allocation). This item is required. The internal procedure employed by the implementor does not have to be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (12.4.6.4, SAME clause, General rule 4b)
